prerequisites: Physics in 2nd year of Bachillerato (Spanish high school)
Derivation and integration of single-variable functions

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the concept of a wave and know its mathematical characterization as well as basic wave phenomena.
Know the basic concepts and laws of electromagnetism and apply them to the analysis of simple electromagnetic situations in vacuum and in material media.
Correctly handle the recommended physical symbology, both in terms of magnitudes and units.
Learn and apply problem-solving strategies related to the different contents of the course.
Acquire skills related to laboratory work and the treatment of measurements and errors.

syllabus_topics: Electrostatics: Electric charge, Coulomb's Law, Electrostatic field and potential, Charge distributions, Electric dipole, Gauss's Law, Conductors, Capacitors, Electric field energy, Dielectrics.
Electric Current: Electric current intensity and density, Ohm's Law, Resistance, Joule effect, Generators: Electromotive force, DC circuits.

Magnetostatics: Magnetic field, Lorentz Law: Magnetic induction, Hall effect, Magnetic force on an electric current, Magnetic field moment on a loop, Biot-Savart Law, Force between currents, Ampere's Theorem, Magnetic field energy, Magnetism in matter.
Time-varying electromagnetic fields: Electromagnetic induction: Faraday-Henry Law, Self-induction, Maxwell's Equations, RLC circuits, Electrical oscillations.
Oscillations: Free oscillations, Damped oscillations, Forced oscillations.
Waves: Generalities. Mechanical waves: Concept of wave, Wave differential equation, Wave classification, Harmonic waves, Mechanical waves, Wave phenomena, Sound waves, Doppler effect.
teaching_methods: Expository classes (exposition and explanation of theoretical content, exemplification and problem-solving, group evaluation activities)
Classroom/Seminar practices (problem-solving, group work activities, presentation and defense of problems/works/projects, small group evaluation activities)
Laboratory practices (handling measurement equipment, use of simulation software and/or experimental data processing, analysis of results and report writing, very small group evaluation activities)
Solving problems and preparing reports for individual or group work
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, if minimums for P1 and P2 are met, the theoretical block grade is (0.35 * T1) + (0.40 * T2) + (0.10 * PA). If P1 minimum is not met, it's (0.75 * ET) + (0.10 * PA). For the practical block, it's (0.08 * P1) + (0.07 * P2). To pass, a minimum of 5/10 is required for P1, 4/10 for P2 and ET, and 75% attendance to practical sessions is mandatory. The final grade is the sum of the theoretical and practical blocks, unless the conditions are not met, in which case the grade is the minimum of the calculated grade and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, the theoretical block is (0.75 * ET) + (0.10 * PA) and the practical block grade for students with less than 75% attendance is (0.15 * P2), otherwise previous practical grades are maintained. A minimum of 4/10 is required for ET and P2 in the extraordinary call.
